::: {#sol-bikeshare-temp}

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

##### R

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Scatterplot of the number of bikes rented in an hour
#|   against the temperature.
#|   The points drift upward from left to right,
#|   and the points spread more at warm temperatures than at cold ones.
# Small, faint points, because thousands of hours overlap.
bikeshare_raw |>
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::aes(x = temp, y = bikers) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.3) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Temperature (scaled to 0 to 1)",
    y = "Bikes rented in the hour"
  )
```

##### R (base)

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Scatterplot of the number of bikes rented in an hour
#|   against the temperature.
#|   The points drift upward from left to right,
#|   and the points spread more at warm temperatures than at cold ones.
# Small, faint points, because thousands of hours overlap.
faint_black <- grDevices::adjustcolor("black", alpha.f = 0.3)
plot(
  bikeshare_raw$temp,
  bikeshare_raw$bikers,
  pch = 16,
  cex = 0.3,
  col = faint_black,
  xlab = "Temperature (scaled to 0 to 1)",
  ylab = "Bikes rented in the hour"
)
```

##### Python

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Scatterplot of the number of bikes rented in an hour
#|   against the temperature.
#|   The points drift upward from left to right,
#|   and the points spread more at warm temperatures than at cold ones.
# Small, faint points, because thousands of hours overlap.
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4), layout="constrained")
ax.scatter(bikeshare_raw["temp"], bikeshare_raw["bikers"], s=4, alpha=0.3);
ax.set_xlabel("Temperature (scaled to 0 to 1)");
ax.set_ylabel("Bikes rented in the hour");
plt.show()
```

:::

```{r}
#| include: false
temp_bikers_r <- cor(bikeshare_raw$temp, bikeshare_raw$bikers)
temp_bikers_r_round <- round(temp_bikers_r, 2)
```

The counts rise with the temperature, with [sample correlation](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-pearson-r) `r temp_bikers_r_round`.
The spread of the counts grows with their level.
A [Poisson regression model](poisson-regression.qmd#def-poisson-regression) describes that pattern,
because the [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance) of a [Poisson](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-poisson) variable is the same as its [expected value](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-expectation).

:::
